_readme: Prediction layer for the book-log / book-suggest skills. One JSON object per line, keys matching book-cache.json. Estimates are RECOMPUTED BY /book-log (its PROPAGATE phase), never by /book-suggest, which only reads them. Roughly sorted best-first; the order is a convenience, never load-bearing. Access state is NOT in this file: book-cache.json is authoritative for that and nothing here may duplicate it.
_revs: book-revs.json. Nothing in this header line may contain a literal dep id, so that a grep for one returns book lines only.
_est: [low, high] score range, CONDITIONAL on nothing in 'risks' firing. null means 'blocked' names a hard filter the book already fails.
_deps: dep-id -> the rev in 'revs' this estimate was computed under. Valid iff every dep rev still matches. Mandatory minimum on every line (all with the axis: prefix, spelled out here without it so this note is not itself a grep hit): the three taste hard filters opening, occult and detective; the two heaviest graded axes worldbuilding and protagonist; motives; and the author id. A change to any of those cannot miss a book whose estimate never examined it - the Mortal Engines 55 lesson, where the prediction was argued on the opening and lost on the axis it never looked at. axis:access is deliberately NOT a dep: access lives in book-cache.json only.
_leanedOn: the dep(s) actually carrying the number. A change here means re-derive from scratch; a change to a merely-listed dep usually means no move. Both prediction failures so far - Artemis (predicted 80, scored 76) and Mortal Engines 55 - came from leaning on the wrong axis, and this field is what makes that measurable.
_risks: axis ids that could collapse the estimate below its range. Always a subset of deps. Must be stated when the book is proposed.
_invariant: one line here for every book in book-cache.json, and vice versa; no line for a book in books-read.md.
_depth: 'deep' marks a line re-derived by /book-deep from a sourced per-axis dossier in book-deep.jsonl; absent means screening depth. A deep line is re-priced from its dossier when a rule moves, never re-derived from scratch.

why: Dived against the Czech Host edition, whose order matches the English: the alchemist's-gate story first, the title story second, a seven-minute piece on determinism third, then the long digient novella. A collection is decided at its front, and here the front is the strongest part, the reverse of Já, robot 55. The opening story was read in the publisher's excerpt: one narrator, one concrete scene, his grief stated on page one, and the tale Czech readers most often call the best. Its lead faces a past cruelty and refuses to be that man again, the clause Světlo věcí konečných 96 was liked for, and it takes fate and belief seriously inside its own declared rule, mocking neither. The title story is the heaviest axis done exactly: one declared mechanism followed to the end of its world, what Project Hail Mary 92 was praised for. The deductions sit behind the front. The fourth story is close to a third of the book, slow, told rather than shown, and the commonest complaint; momentum dips the way Počítání hvězd 85 did; the eighth story makes faith its subject, seriously but not as a thread; and the first story's third tale wraps a short, tasteful seduction in the trappings of an affair, though the lover is the wife's own husband. A high peak, several small pushbacks, and none of the three causes that ended Já, robot 55.

The closest structural analogue to Seeking Allah 91 anywhere in the catalogue: first-person account of leaving Islam, examined belief plus insight into how another group experiences the world - the two things that actually earned that 91, not the memoir form itself, which Anne Frank 40 discredited. Risks are real bleakness and drift toward argument.

Linked stories carrying declared consequences across a whole arc, and the idea is nameable: colonisation written as elegy rather than adventure. The arc is what earns - each story pays for the one before it, which is the structure face of the heaviest axis, priced by the Tolkien gradient from Silmarillion 80 down to Unfinished Tales 69. Short form removes penalties rather than adding points, so the range rests on the ideas and the arc and not on the length. Bleakness is a mild pushback: the elegiac register is sustained, and 1984 60 is the only book in the log grim enough to have cost real points. Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. Linked stories with one arc are the least exposed shape after Ja, robot, since each piece pays for the one before it rather than starting from nothing - the structure face the Tolkien gradient prices from Silmarillion 80 down to Unfinished Tales 69. The trim is for the front of the book specifically: it opens on very short vignettes before the arc is legible, and an opening that has not yet declared what it is doing is where this reader stops.
Contemporary, contested, first-person Uyghur testimony - the Qureshi 91 axis rather than the historical-canon form that failed. Bleakness is genuine here and is a mild pushback only.

t: Cekam, az si pro me v noci prijdou
why: A poet's account of getting his family out of Xinjiang ahead of arrest. The memoir form earns nothing by itself - Anne Frank 40 is the same form and failed outright - so this rests on the two things that did earn: examining what is actually true, and insight into how another group experiences the world, the axis behind Seeking Allah 91 and Son of Hamas 75. The surveillance state is documented at the level of one family's decisions, with more interiority than the reportage form usually carries. Bleakness is the standing risk, though 1984 60 is the only book grim enough to have cost real points.

Society as subject with the premise followed through rigorously. Bleak, but the Animal Farm 78 model of bleak-with-ideas rather than immersion in misery, and the child leads are suspended by the short-idea-driven rule.

Short allegory in the Little Prince 82 shape, but the resemblance is formal and the ideas are not. Name the idea and it comes out as 'pursue mastery for its own sake', delivered in an earnest new-age register - thin next to what actually earned the Little Prince its 82. Re-derived 2026-08-26: this was floated on the category rather than on its content, which the sharpened rule no longer allows.

A Syrian monk held by IS - faith carried inside a narrative, which is the stated preference exactly. Risk is the balance tipping from story to devotional reflection, which is the no-theology-as-subject line. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:faith appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.

Vonnegut's early slick-magazine work, written to sell to Collier's rather than to argue anything - the voice is there, the ideas are not, and this is explicitly not the canonical Vonnegut. A cheap way to test the author, not a book with a case of its own. Re-derived 2026-08-26. Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. This was already argued as the author's uncanonical magazine work, ideas absent and voice present, and it was priced as a cheap way to test him. It is no longer cheap: a collection is put down on its weakest early pieces, and a book explicitly assembled from work written to sell rather than to argue has no reason to put its best foot forward.

t: Pribehy vaseho zivota (Stories of Your Life and Others)
why: Downgraded again 2026-09-03, and the reason the earlier downgrade was not enough is now a rule. The occult breach stands: one story takes its golem-animation straight from real Kabbalistic and Hermetic name-magic and stages the inscribing rite on the page, so both tests fail, and occult is the most severe objection in the log with its three failures sitting at 51, 53 and 57. What held this well above them was the argument that the breach is one story of eight and is skippable. That argument is now dead: Ja, robot 55 is a collection the reader put down after three stories rather than reading around the ones that did not work, and it establishes that a multi-story book is experienced from the front and abandoned on its weakest early pieces. A second deduction rides on the same finding - one of these stories is literal theodicy, faith as the subject rather than a thread inside a story, and the reader's own words about the collection he abandoned name a religious treatment he disliked. The rest is one premise per story followed to its end, every idea nameable in a phrase, and that is why this is not lower still.

Genuine philosophical weight - the Ridiculous Man's dream is an idea, not a mood - so it survives the sharpened rule. Risks are the 19th-century Russian register and openings that circle before they land: legible, but not immediately gripping, which is the axis the log is most sensitive to. Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. The philosophical weight is real and the best-known piece here is an idea rather than a mood, but that piece is the case for the whole book and it is not first. The range was set by it; under the new axis it cannot be, and the openings that circle before they land - already the stated risk - are what the reader would meet first.

Immediately legible Edwardian comic stories, and humour is not the objection (cf. Adams 83). But the stories trade on wit and a last-line reversal and leave nothing behind, which is the axis the log is most consistent about - 'wants higher things to think about' is the most common reason a competent book stalls in the 60s. Re-derived 2026-08-26; being short bought it nothing. Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. Short comic pieces with a cruel twist, uniform in method, so the front of the book resembles the rest of it - which limits the damage. The trim is for what uniformity cannot fix: there is no arc, nobody recurs, and a book put down after three pieces has seen the whole method already.

t: Vrchol vulkanu (The Top of the Volcano)
why: Award-winning short SF with genuine per-story ideas, which survives the sharpened rule - but a self-selected career retrospective is uneven by construction, and the confrontational register carries real sexual-violence content on the axis that actually costs. Re-derived 2026-08-26. Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. A New Wave selection is the shape most exposed to this axis: deliberately varied, deliberately transgressive, with the anthologised famous pieces scattered through it rather than placed first. The sexual-treatment risk already on this line is the second reason the front of the book cannot be assumed benign, and crudeness is the one dimension of that axis the log actually anchors, at Ready Player One 55.
Sequel to the two highest scores in the log (95, 92) with the protagonist already proven; discounted for the sequels-are-not-safe rule and Brown's own 95->92 slope.
Clears occult, worldbuilding and prophecy; Vin is a rootable lead with real interiority. Held under 90 by heavy exposition and an ideas ceiling.

Part 1 is the opening this reader asks for: one man climbing to his death, and chapter one already says who Holston is, why he chose it and what it costs. The leads who die hand over to people met a part earlier, so investment moves rather than restarts, and Juliette is rootable with real flaws. The silo's society is the subject and it holds as a control system; the visor lie is planted in Part 1 and paid off in Part 3, the earned reveal of Golden Son 92. Readers split on whether the lie keeps people alive, the higher-things axis behind Animal Farm 78, and the ending relieves rather than crushes, so the 1984 60 objection stays shut. Against it, fans and critics alike report a sag from the mayor's descent to around page 200, stair padding included; Počítání hvězd 85 shows missing drive costs a few points, not a band, and the descent is interior, the Red Rising 95 strength. Part 3 is a sheriff working closed deaths and deleted files, which several Czech readers call a detective story: a flagged strand, a light dock. The physical face has gaps the book never closes (no lift in a 144-level shaft, improvised guns, decades-old food in a dead silo), peripheral to the premise unlike Mortal Engines 55, and Juliette's later survivals read to some as plot armour. Hunger Games 89 is the shape, looser in pace. Discovery (axis:discovery, added 2026-10-24, not part of the dive and priced the screening way): the one forbidden question, what is outside, is the book, survival depends on the answer, and the answer arrives and fits what was planted, all three conditions of the shape the reader named in Project Hail Mary 92 and Stín věcí ztracených 93; central, so +4.

t: Leva ruka tmy (The Left Hand of Darkness)
why: Ideas and motives carry it. With sex taken out of politics it asks what is left of loyalty and love, sets patriotism against fear of the other, and has a religion foretell only to show the uselessness of answers; page time goes to what people want, misread motive in the first half and two people learning each other on the ice, the shape that put Speaker for the Dead at 90. The world carries its declared biology into politics, and Genly is a lead with flaws he outgrows. Then four deductions. The Handdara Foretelling is a working rite of an invented, godless religion, staged once with the narrator in the circle: moderate, five points off both ends. The first half is slow and name-dense, the missing drive that held Pocitani hvezd to 85, and readers say it takes off only with the escape. The opening is one legible thread, glossed as it goes but heavy with terms, a point or two. And the emotional core is an unconsummated love between the narrator and a character the Czech text makes grammatically male, a lighter case of what cost Caropisci 67 but one a single anchor cannot size, so the range is wide at the bottom. Bleakness is mild: the ice is shared and the death buys the mission, nearer Project Hail Mary 92 than 1984 60. Standalone. Discovery (axis:discovery, 2026-10-24, not part of the dive and priced the screening way): an envoy arrives alone on a world he does not understand, must understand it to do his job and then to survive the ice, and the answer fits, the arrival case the reader named beside Project Hail Mary 92; partly credited above as two people learning each other, so partial, +2.

OPENING, read in the publisher's sample of all of Part One: one man, one job, one encounter. A fireman burns a house full of books, rides home and meets a seventeen-year-old neighbour, and within a few pages the reader knows that firemen start fires and reading is against the law. Thick with metaphor and never unclear, so neither Guards! Guards! 30 nor the Čaropisci 67 opening. CASE: the idea fits in a sentence, a public that gave up reading for speed, screens and not giving offence and now burns what is left so nobody feels unequal, and the captain who explains it does so in a way that holds. The lead travels the way Caeden did in Stín věcí ztracených 93, from 'It was a pleasure to burn' to the man who carries Ecclesiastes in his head. 1984 60 ends with its man broken; this ends with the walk back to a bombed city to rebuild, and Czech readers set the two apart on exactly that. COSTS: the first third is the best of it, the middle runs on speeches, the close is quick, and a minority find the Czech text clumsy or confused in the escape. Fireproof houses that still burn and a war that lands the night of the escape are the world snags readers raise, small beside Divergent 58. Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82 are the floor and the ceiling.

The opening was read in the author's own sample: one room, one lesson that explains minister, Gettland and the gods as it goes, then the news that makes Yarvi king. That is one thread with full context, so the opening bar is clear. Momentum carries the book, the Hunger Games 89 shape: one viewpoint, short, read in a sitting by most reviewers. Yarvi has flaws to beat (self-pity, cowardice, a maimed hand) and constant interiority, and the closing reveal is planted on page one, earned the way Golden Son 92 earned its own. The ceiling is ideas: maxims about the lesser evil and the greater good rather than a question worked through, nearer The Hobbit 84 than Mockingjay 91, and readers keep calling it simple. Then four small deductions. The first third reads teen from the inside, self-pitying and passive, the Ender's Game 87 cost. A royal ship-funeral staged in chapter four slaughters two dozen horses for an invented god of death. Nothing in the book is magic and its miracles are shown to be faked, so this is graded rather than vetoed, but the reader should hear of it first. A long-lost uncle happens to be chained on the same galley, the authorial luck Valka stareho muze 87 was praised for refusing. Doves are trained to talk. Volume 1, with a closed arc.

Volume 1, its own arc closed. The ceiling is the premise face of the heaviest axis at Project Hail Mary 92 height: chapter one declares what the uplift virus does, and the book follows its consequences for millennia through a spider civilisation whose tech, politics and faith all grow from its body, ending in a first-contact conflict settled by understanding rather than extermination, the shape Speaker for the Dead 90 was liked for. What holds it below that is the people. The most repeated complaint, Czech and English, is that the humans are cold, Holsten has little agency and nobody is easy to root for; the spider leads are generational role-names, so the rooting goes to a species and its causes. Artemis 69 forbids predicting up on the world when the lead is thin, and this range does not; but the book is not built around one lead, and The Silmarillion 80 shows a people's chronicle can score without one. Momentum costs a few points as in Počítání hvězd 85: a slow first half, a fast last fifth. Faith is serious rather than satirical but deflationary, the god a half-mad satellite and religion outgrown, between Světlo věcí konečných 96 and Já, robot 55. Opening clear on the excerpt; occult, sexual content and detective clear. Discovery (axis:discovery, 2026-10-24, not part of the dive and priced the screening way): partial, a search for a home and a rediscovered past rather than an unknown the book is built on, and the people are the open doubt, so it prices at nothing; the number holds.
Testimony about what is true - the Qureshi 91 pattern, not the bare form Anne Frank 40 discredited. Risks are camp bleakness (mild) and a theory-heavy back half that edges toward theory-as-subject.

The same author's Little Prince scored 82 and these carry the same reflective register, with real ideas about duty, solitude and what men owe each other. Kept high on the author's proven record rather than on the form; trimmed slightly because the form itself no longer adds.

Heavy interiority and a staggered chapter-per-POV opening, both confirmed acceptable. Two live risks: First Law's crude sexual material (the axis that actually costs, and the 'only occasional' defence is void), and rootability - Glokta is a torturer, which is the Ballad 65 failure mode. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:protagonist appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.
Single legible first-person with personhood as its idea, and short enough to sit in the idea-driven category. Access is the open question, not fit.

A single protagonist in first person with a want the whole plot runs on - the axis that outranks worldbuilding whenever the two compete (Artemis 69) - and he is hiding who he is from the academy training him. A lead whose past is the open question is what the reader named as his favourite thing in Licanius 92-96, where uncovering who Caeden was, and the uncertainty while it lasted, carried the series. Here the reader shares the secret from the first page, so it is concealment rather than discovery and should pay less than it did there. A declared power system the society is visibly organised around: ceding will buys status, so the hierarchy is a consequence of the rule rather than decoration - the declared-capability test passed, the axis Hunger Games 89 and Ender's Game 87 both score on. Same author as Licanius, whose twists the reader found consistent with everything before them across three volumes - the heaviest axis met at the top score in the log. But an author's record is a prior on his named works and never a licence, and within-author spreads in this log run to 26 points (Collins 91 to 65), so the range rises without inheriting. Raised from [76, 84] on 2026-10-24 for that record, and because the prophecy risk it was held under is gone: how central fate is costs nothing, only how it is handled. Access is the constraint, not fit. Since 2026-10-24 the concealment credited above is priced as axis:discovery, once and not raised: the reader shares the secret, and the trilogy is unfinished, so its larger questions are not yet answered; the number holds.

Canonical short SF, and individual stories will land well. But an anthology has no single idea to name and averages toward its middle, so there is nothing to predict it up on: the short-form suspension removes penalties and never adds points, and canonicity is not a positive case (Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82 earn on their ideas, not their status). The real argument is cheap breadth across a dozen authors, which is a reason to read it next rather than a reason to expect a high score. Re-derived 2026-08-26. Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. A multi-author hall-of-fame anthology has no single premise, and its case was always breadth rather than a bet. Under the new axis breadth is worth less than it was: the reader does not average a collection, he reads it from the front, so twenty good stories do not compensate for two early ones that do not land.

One strong nameable idea - a community that abolished pain, choice and colour, and what inheriting its memories costs - with the premise followed through. Survives the sharpened rule; trimmed because the YA register and the child lead are now unoffset. Discovery (axis:discovery, 2026-10-24): the memories the lead inherits are the unknown, and once they show him what the community hides he has to act, the memory-and-world shape of Project Hail Mary 92 and Stín věcí ztracených 93. Partial rather than central: the book reveals what the community hides but leaves the world beyond it and its own ending open, so +2.

PROVISIONAL - contents unverified, and the sharpened rule means an unverified short collection can no longer be floated on the category alone. Sanderson clears occult, worldbuilding and prophecy, but clearing filters is not a positive case. Wide range because the contents genuinely decide it; check the shelf before proposing. Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. Contents unverified in this catalogue, which was already noted and is now a larger problem than it was: an unverified table of contents is an unverified opening, and the opening is what decides whether a collection survives its first hour.

The strongest worldbuilding case available - one invented drive and the whole civilisation reorganises around water, air and g-tolerance - and two anchored POVs, so the opening clears. Wide range because half the book is Miller working a missing-person case, adjacent to the one hard-avoided genre.
A society that has abolished death and must administer it - premise declared and followed through. YA register and teen leads are small pushbacks.

Declares less than Mistborn does, so less binds it, and the Defiant caste order does follow from the war. Drags: YA register, teen pilot lead, training-school structure - a lower ceiling than Mistborn but no English needed. Discovery (axis:discovery, 2026-10-24): the derelict ship, what her father really did and what the planet once was are uncovered alongside the flight school, the shape of Stín věcí ztracených 93 at smaller scale; partial because the school is the spine, so +2.

Short, first-person, legible from page one, collapse premise worked out. Low ceiling but the lowest risk on the list - narrow range on purpose. Discovery (axis:discovery, 2026-10-24): a man wakes to a world changed overnight that he knows nothing about and has to learn its new rules to survive, the arrival case the reader named beside Project Hail Mary 92; partial, because why it happened is left uncertain, so +2.

Anchored on Monte Cristo 75 from the same author: historical, so reality binds, but loose with history without stating false claims as fact. Vivid ensemble and the same momentum; digression is the only real drag.

Undertakes to explain and honours it - the park declares its control rules and the plot is those rules failing as declared. Not predicted up on that: functional thin characters and a set-piece second half are the Artemis shape.

Runs on banking and grain rather than battle, so it is motive-forward by construction - page time on what people want and why, the axis Mockingjay 91 tops the log on - and no strand of it is an investigation, so the hard filter stays clear. Sprawling and slow is the cost: a thin story spread over many pages is the density penalty that capped LOTR 84 and docked Monte Cristo 75. Ideas are the second risk - the politics are absorbing while they run, and there may be nothing to take away afterwards.

Canon and idea-dense, and the range assumes the opening holds. Re-derived 2026-08-28: it probably does not, and that is no longer a caveat. In medias res with unexplained jargon is the hard clarity filter, and that exact configuration has now been read and scored - Caropisci 30, abandoned in chapter one, a heist already running whose invented vocabulary and factions arrived unexplained, on a book that was the strongest unread SF-F pick on the shelf when it was proposed. Gibson does the same thing harder and on purpose, and the disorientation is the point rather than a threshold to cross. The number is unchanged because the range is conditional on the risk not firing, and averaging a hard filter into a hedge is what this file forbids: this is a 75 or a 30, not a 55. What changed is the probability, and the Author row is now Avoid-unless-asked rather than Revisit.

t: Pilire zeme (The Pillars of the Earth)
why: The plot is a multi-decade saga of building a cathedral against political intrigue, war and family betrayal, not a sexual relationship, so the sex-as-the-plot filter does not fire. The consequence-worked cathedral-building plot and multi-character motive structure are a real positive case, comparable to the historical-epic band this reader has liked: Count of Monte Cristo 75, Les Miserables 71, Exodus 68, Quo Vadis 66. Held at this range on 2026-08-28 with the comparator corrected. Ruled 2026-08-28: The Witcher 53 is a CONFOUNDED row and cannot be cited as a sexual-axis floor - the reader named two independent causes, 'both magic (witches) and the sex was through out the series', and the magic is the occult filter, the most severe objection in the log. The clean crudeness anchor is Ready Player One 55 - 'it was the kind of sex that reduced it that much', the kind and not the amount - with Artemis 69 confirming crudeness costs even in small doses. VOLUME IS UNANCHORED and must not be priced as cheap: Red Rising 95 and Valka stareho muze 87 are BOTH low volume on the reader's own account ('mostly one chapter of a book'), so neither shows what sustained non-crude content costs, and the log's only high-volume row is the confounded one. Note also that VSM's single chapter was still enough to become his one named complaint, so light volume is not free. The correction does not rescue this book, because the dimension it downgrades is not the one doing the work here: the treatment is described as fixated on the mechanics of rape to the point of being gratuitous, which is the crudeness dimension at its worst and is the Ready Player One charge at far greater length. Volume then compounds it rather than causing it.

t: Naslouchej nozi (The Knife of Never Letting Go)
why: One declared premise - audible thoughts - worked out consistently. Risk is the stylised dialect first-person opening: legible but unusual, and clarity is the hard filter. Teen lead and grimness are small pushbacks. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:opening appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.

The LitRPG game-mechanics ideas are real - a dungeon run as a televised system with declared rules that the plot then obeys - and they keep this off the floor of the C band. But a mid-70s ceiling built on ideas alone cannot survive this much crude sexual content stacked on top. Held on 2026-08-28 with the comparator corrected. Ruled 2026-08-28: The Witcher 53 is a CONFOUNDED row and cannot be cited as a sexual-axis floor - the reader named two independent causes, 'both magic (witches) and the sex was through out the series', and the magic is the occult filter, the most severe objection in the log. The clean crudeness anchor is Ready Player One 55 - 'it was the kind of sex that reduced it that much', the kind and not the amount - with Artemis 69 confirming crudeness costs even in small doses. VOLUME IS UNANCHORED and must not be priced as cheap: Red Rising 95 and Valka stareho muze 87 are BOTH low volume on the reader's own account ('mostly one chapter of a book'), so neither shows what sustained non-crude content costs, and the log's only high-volume row is the confounded one. Note also that VSM's single chapter was still enough to become his one named complaint, so light volume is not free. The Ready Player One half of the old comparison is the half that applies, and it applies directly: pervasive, graphic and crude at once is that charge at greater length.

Reopened 2026-08-31 on Mort 83: the prose-style discount this line carried is gone, so the range rises from [70, 79] and this is a real proposal rather than a retest. Ideas carry it - a boy and a girl rebuilding a wiped-out island nation, with whether the gods exist and what makes a people the declared subject, worked out rather than asserted, which is the earner behind Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82 and the thing Narnia 67 was marked down for lacking; belief stays a thread inside a survival story rather than becoming the subject, so it sits on the right side of the faith preference. Opening verdict: one concrete situation the reader has the context to read - a wave, an emptied island, one survivor - with no invented vocabulary to decode, the opposite of the roughly six simultaneous thread starts that produced The Colour of Magic 30 and Guards! Guards! 30, and it is the same authorial voice that scored 83. World verdict: a near-real-world alternate 1860s Pacific with nothing supernatural declared as a mechanism, so reality binds and it holds; the alternate British succession is a device and is the one thin spot on the fact face. Risks: the YA crossover register, which costs heavily only where there is no adult layer to grade and here there is one; and the lead, who spends the first stretch in grief and acted upon rather than wanting something, the Oliver Twist 57 exposure. Ceiling is the comic-fantasy A band rather than above it - Hitchhiker's Guide 83 and Saturnin 78 both score on voice and character - with one nameable idea set on top of that.
Accessible and funny with a legible single voice, but easy-but-shallow is a known mid-70s ceiling. Access is the constraint, not fit.

Light comic standalone with clear prose and a legible opening - a Hollywood agent hired to represent the first aliens to make contact, one situation stated on page one. RAISED 2026-08-28 on a real score rather than a guess: Valka stareho muze 87 confirms the prose is clear and the openings legible, and retires the 'nothing to think about, ceiling near 70' worry that held the old range down. It does not transfer wholesale - that book earned its 87 on a worked-out premise and an alien culture taken seriously, and this is a comedy with a slighter idea, which is the Hitchhiker's Guide 83 shape at a lower altitude. The top assumes the comic voice carries it; the floor is the competent-but-thin B band.
Worldbuilding fails on form two: it undertakes to explain in real quantum vocabulary, so real physics binds it, and it handles that loosely. Thriller pacing carries it but it is thin on motive.

Momentum and a premise stated plainly - memory as a place you can go back to - and the motive engine is unusually clear for a thriller: a father who lost a daughter, a scientist whose mother is losing herself, each wanting one thing for the whole book. That is what holds it in the B band. The deduction is the second form of the heaviest axis: Crouch undertakes to explain the mechanism in real vocabulary, so the explanation becomes binding, and the rules bend to suit each act rather than holding under thought. Access is the constraint as well.

Re-derived 2026-10-24 under the re-ruled occult filter; it now grades instead of blocking. Source passes: the six Divinities are the book's own, with no real god or rite behind them, and the miracle shown in full, Olvos's frost, is worked by licking a finger and writing on a pane to open a speaking line home, with no invocation or prayer. But the power is granted by gods, so the mechanism escape fails, and the lead works miracles repeatedly and channels them through relics at the climax: heavy, ten off both ends. No human sacrifice is staged. Start from Čaropisci 67, same author, whose world and leads he liked: this world is built the same way, one declared event (the gods' deaths) whose consequences are the setting, and its ideas on conquest and erased history are stronger. Shara is rootable, a loyal spy who ends up choosing the truth over her ministry, though one strong critic found her never fully alive. Against it: the courtroom opening is a wall of unfamiliar names, so propose it premise-first; a major secondary character is a closeted gay man, the light end of that axis; the first half is slow. Two risks sit outside the range. A spy works a murder case for most of the book, which Czech readers call a detective story; if that counts, this is a bar. And the gods prove shaped by their believers, told seriously, but devout faith shows mostly as oppression.

Czech original, so no translation route needed. The whole book is why Hana became who she is - the motives axis directly, which is the axis that separates Mockingjay 91 from Catching Fire 83. Historical, so reality binds, and the 1954 typhus epidemic it turns on is real and researched: the fact face passes. Set in the reader's own town. Risks: Holocaust plus epidemic is heavy, and the first section is narrated by a child. SCREENED 2026-09-02 on axis:sex-portrayal, verdict mild, was [78, 86]. A deliberately female-line family saga: a review notes Mornstajnova looks at her men only from outside and does not work with their psyche, and the two adult men who matter come off poorly - Karel Karasek the closed, selfish watchmaker and Jaroslav Horacek, who used Hana and lacked the nerve to leave her cleanly. Held to mild because the deficit is moral and emotional rather than competence, Gusta Horacek is drawn as honourable, and the women are survivors rather than the clever ones. The dock is the profile's stated convention (mild -2, moderate -5), not a measured magnitude - the axis has no high-contrast anchor yet.

Genuinely idea-dense: the 20th century told as a flat catalogue of its own statistics and atrocities, which is an argument about how the century narrated itself. Survives the sharpened rule on that. But it has no protagonist and no narrative line, and the deadpan accumulation is a structural and bleakness risk rather than a free pass. Re-derived 2026-08-26.

Short novella whose whole plot is a con - a group paying for a rescue that was never going to happen - so it is built on weighing what is believable, the rigour credited for Seeking Allah 91. Risk: unrelieved bleakness, and the Anne Frank 40 precedent shows the Holocaust subject earns nothing by itself.

Four narrators, staggered rather than simultaneous, so the opening still clears, and the political material - expulsion, penal labour, a friend's crisis of faith - is idea-dense in the way that lifts a book out of the 60s. But the revenge plot's climax is an extended, weighted seduction scene, not a brief or incidental one, and the corrected axis prices that length and explicitness on their own terms - coldness of tone is not the same as it being restrained or small in volume, which is what the previous note assumed when it called the treatment clinical and left the axis unpriced. The essayistic digressions remain a separate, smaller density penalty in the Les Miserables 71 mould.

Screened and recorded low rather than dropped, because it fails on a graded axis, not a filter. First-person slow descent into evil with nobody to root for - the exact Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes 65 shape, which cost 22 points against Sunrise 87 on the protagonist alone. Being short and idea-driven (how a mild man becomes a monster) is the only thing holding it this high. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:protagonist appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.

Re-derived 2026-09-03 on this author's first real score. Ja, robot 55 was abandoned three stories in and the reader's first complaint was that the opening story had nobody to root for. That is this book's own known shape rather than an accident of that collection: the sections jump decades and change cast, so nobody is on the page long enough to want something the reader can follow. The earlier range priced 'no continuous lead' as survivable against Silmarillion 80, and that comparison is now the weaker of the two available - Silmarillion is myth that never promises a protagonist, while this keeps introducing people and dropping them, which is the thing that has just cost this author a real score. What holds it in the B band rather than dropping it further is genuine: psychohistory is declared precisely and the decline is worked out as its consequence, the premise face the reader volunteered as a positive in Old Man's War 87, and almost all the page time is people talking and scheming rather than acting, the axis that puts Mockingjay 91 and Speaker for the Dead 90 at the top of the log. Leaned on the protagonist because a thin or absent lead outranks a strong world - Artemis 69 settled that - and this is the second time that rule has had to be applied to this author, not the first.

Every page is inside one mind: Charlie's progress reports carry what he wants, fears and remembers, the axis behind Red Rising 95 and Speaker for the Dead 90. The novel adds what the story lacked, his own past surfacing memory by memory, the element singled out in Stín věcí ztracených 93, and a real flaw to face: the genius turns arrogant and he turns back toward warmth before the end, the direction-of-travel case, not The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes 65. The ideas are nameable and left open: intelligence without emotional growth, a man treated as a lab animal by the people who made him. The opening is one situation with its context in the first paragraph, misspelt but never confusing, and the one declared rule is obeyed: Algernon's decline sets up Charlie's. Three costs. Sex is a recurring thread, not a chapter: Freudian rather than crude, so not the Ready Player One 55 kind, but more than the single chapter that became the one complaint on Válka starého muže 87, and volume is unmeasured, so the range stays wide. The sadness is gradual and humane, nearer the loneliness dock of The Martian 82 than 1984 60. And Czech readers keep finding the middle padded and the arc foreseeable, the drive complaint of Počítání hvězd 85. Standalone. Since 2026-10-24 the surfacing past credited above is priced as axis:discovery (not part of the dive), once: partial, a side effect of the surgery rather than something he must find out; the number holds.

A tour boat sinks under a lunar dust sea and the rest is engineering against a clock: the shape of The Martian 82 more than Project Hail Mary 92, with problems solved but no Rocky and no sacrifice. The dust is declared once (dry, fine, flowing like water) and obeyed: trapped heat kills the air scrubber, waste turns dust to mud and starts a second cave-in, dust in the hull starts a fire. Readers say the setbacks never feel contrived, so the world earns as Weir's did. Against The Martian it gains two things the reader docked there, a group trapped together instead of one man alone and a tense last-minute finish instead of a dragging end, and it gives back the lead. Pat Harris is likeable, doubts that he handed command over too easily and nearly botches the air line, so this is not the one-note lead of Artemis 69; but the cast is lightly drawn and the page time goes on the work, not on what people want. The 1961 women cost a little: the stewardess is capable, the others are a soured spinster and an ex-dancer played for laughs, the reverse of the contrast the reader objects to and of unmeasured size. The opening sets up one boat, one crew and one sea before anything goes wrong, and the rescuers arrive one viewpoint at a time. One veiled love scene, no occult, and the detective aboard is a one-scene reveal. Standalone.

Unspace is declared with rules and the rules are then what the plot runs on - a declared capability whose consequences the book actually carries, the axis Project Hail Mary 92 and Ender's Game 87 both score on. Idris is the reason not to lean on the world alone: an Intermediary with a concrete want and a cost he keeps paying, so the Artemis 69 trap of predicting up on worldbuilding over a thin lead does not apply on the evidence. The floor drops on re-derivation though, because Artemis was revised down on 2026-08-27: the penalty for the protagonist risk firing is now measurably worse than it looked, and this range is conditional on that risk not firing. The other risk is the ensemble of crew POVs - they braid in after Idris is established rather than starting at once, which is the LOTR 84 pattern and not the Guards! Guards! 30 one, but there are enough of them to matter.

t: Muz, ktery si pletl manzelku s kloboukem (The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat)
why: Hits the non-fiction earner exactly as the profile states it: examining what is actually true, plus insight into how another group experiences the world. Anne Frank 40 failed because bare testimony earns nothing; Sacks is the opposite case, every chapter a short idea-driven piece with a nameable question. Case-study form means the character rules are suspended without needing the suspension. Density is the only risk - the neurological apparatus can crowd the story out.

Short, single-protagonist, one idea declared and worked out to its end - that wisdom cannot be transmitted, only lived. That is the The Little Prince 82 shape at the higher end, because the idea is harder and the protagonist actually changes rather than serving as a vehicle for it. Motives are the entire text. On the occult filter: asceticism and meditation are practised on the page but no deity is petitioned and nothing supernatural is enacted, so it does not fire. Faith is the graded risk instead - what the profile wants is religion carried inside a story (Seeking Allah 91, Son of Hamas 75) rather than as a subject in its own right, and this sits close to that boundary.

Fiction doing the thing that earned Seeking Allah 91 and Son of Hamas 75: insight into how another group experiences the world, from inside. Guilt and its attempted repair is the engine, so page time goes to what Amir wants and why rather than what he does. Flawed-but-rootable lead, single thread, clear opening. The risk is severity rather than bleakness of tone - there is a child rape and it is not softened; the treatment is serious rather than crude, which is the axis that matters here, but it is the one thing that could sink this below the range.

Ninety pages, one protagonist, and the private humiliation is what drives the public act - motives over action with nothing else in the way, which is the axis Mockingjay 91 tops the log on. The idea is nameable in a phrase, so the short form is not what is carrying it. Deliberately not leaned on protagonist: Milos is interesting throughout but only becomes rootable at the end. Bleakness is a mild pushback at most - Animal Farm 78 is bleak and pays nothing for it. An audio edition exists (Supraphon 2009, Krystof Hadek) alongside four print ones.

Seldon is on the page from the first chapter to the last, so the science arrives as one man's problem rather than as scaffolding the reader is told about - a continuous protagonist with a concrete want, which is the axis that outranks worldbuilding whenever the two compete (Artemis 69). Trimmed 2026-09-03 on this author's first real score: Ja, robot 55 was put down three stories in, and the complaint that ended it was a cast nobody could root for. This volume is the one holding of his that structurally answers that complaint, which is why it is trimmed by a few points rather than a band - but a real score now says his people are the exposure, and the older range was written when they were only a theoretical risk. Still held out of the A band because this is late work written backwards into a finished shelf: the ideas are retrofitted rather than generative, and the capital is toured more than it is worked out, which is the thin-story-per-page deduction that cancelled LOTR 84's advantage.

One premise - an outpatient procedure that makes couples emotionally telepathic - and Willis takes its social consequences seriously enough that the comedy comes out of the rules rather than around them. That is the worldbuilding axis being paid rather than dodged. Rootable lead, single thread, clear opening. Risk is Willis's screwball method: farce runs on interruption and missed connection, and 500 pages of it is where the thin-story-spread-thin penalty would land. Romance is central but not the point and is not crudely handled.

Leaves ideas behind, which is the profile's own phrase, and the HAL section is pure motive - why a machine that cannot lie starts lying. Clarke's physics is declared and kept. Two deductions: nobody in it is rootable, and the last act deliberately stops explaining after the book has spent 200 pages explaining everything, which is the undertook-to-explain breach rather than the vague-magic exemption. Odeon 1982 is the older print route if the Argo edition is out. Discovery (axis:discovery, 2026-10-24): the journey toward the signal is the spine, but the last act withholds the answer, which forfeits the lift; the number holds.

The idea is nameable in a phrase - whether a nation that has forgotten its atrocity should be made to remember - and the mist is a declared mechanism the book obeys. Axl and Beatrice are a rootable pair with one clear want. The dragon and the ogres are invented, so the occult filter does not fire. Risk is pace: Ishiguro writes it deliberately flat and dreamlike, which is the closest thing here to heavy description with little story in it. Discovery (axis:discovery, 2026-10-24): the couple recover their own forgotten past and the land's at once, need it to find their son, and the answer about the mist arrives and fits, the memory-and-world shape of Stín věcí ztracených 93 and Project Hail Mary 92; central, so +4. Pace remains the risk.

Two hundred pages narrated by a foetus who overhears his mother plotting his father's murder - one conceit, declared on page one, obeyed throughout, which is the short idea-driven category at its safest. The killers' motives are the whole content. On the detective filter: the reader knows who and why from the start, so this is the inverse of a mystery, not an instance of one. Risk is that the narrator physically cannot act, and a protagonist with no agency is a thinner proposition than a thin protagonist.

Motives over action is not a feature of this book, it is the method - almost nothing happens except people calculating, and Cromwell is both interesting and, unusually for him, rootable. Historical fiction lands fine for this reader (Quo Vadis 66, Exodus 68) and this is far better written than either. The opening is the real risk and it is a genuine one: Mantel writes an unsignalled 'he' for Cromwell and drops a large Tudor cast in without introduction, which is a different failure from simultaneous threads but produces the same first-chapter confusion that ended Mortal Engines 55.

One premise stated plainly - every unlived life is a book you can try - with a rootable lead and a nameable idea, read quickly. Risk is on the heaviest axis: the library's rules are thin and Haig leans on them constantly, which is exactly the combination the profile penalises (obligation scales with how hard the book leans, not what it is about). If the rules turn out to bend for the plot this drops into the 60s.

A mother searching for the child taken from her - one want stated plainly and pursued for the whole book, the motives-over-action axis at its most direct (Mockingjay 91). Held below the A band because the engine is the search rather than a single idea worked out, and this log pays for ideas above emotion: Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82 both earn on an idea nameable in a phrase, and this one is 'find the child'. Sequels are not safe bets either - Hitchhiker's 83 to 70. Life-phase proximity is a small pushback at most, never a tier.

A single monologue by a man reconstructing why his wife killed herself: motives are not a feature of the text, they are the text - the axis Mockingjay 91 and Speaker for the Dead 90 both score on, in fifty pages. The idea is nameable and it is the whole book, so the short form is not carrying it. Bleakness is a mild pushback rather than a filter; 1984 60 is the only book in the log grim enough to have cost real points.

The Petersburg tales - a clerk's diary sliding into madness, a nose with a career of its own. Each piece has an idea nameable in a phrase, which is the bar the short-form rule sets, and it clears that bar on the ideas rather than on being short: the suspension removes penalties (The Little Prince 82's child lead, Animal Farm 78's bleakness) and never adds points. Held under the A band because the pieces do not build on each other, a light version of the Unfinished Tales 69 objection, and because there is nobody in them to root for. Audio edition also exists (Supraphon 2015). Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. The line already deducted for the pieces not building on each other and for nobody in them to root for - a light version of Unfinished Tales 69. Ja, robot 55 makes both deductions heavier rather than lighter, because it is the same pair of objections on a collection the reader actually abandoned, and the second of them fired on the very first story he read.

Re-derived 2026-08-27 against a real score by this author. Promena 58 is the measurement that matters: the same author, the same very short form, and the same two risks - a passive lead who is hard to root for, and bleakness that arrives at once instead of gradually - and both fired, taking it twelve points below what was predicted for it. This story is thinner still: one scene, and the verdict is asserted rather than worked out, so the short-form suspension removes penalties without adding anything. Leaning on the protagonist axis rather than on ideas now, because that is what carried the number down in the read book; the idea is kept in risks because the single image may yet land. Below Divergent 58 at the low end and under Percy Jackson 57 is the honest floor for a device narrator with nothing to root for.

One idea declared and carried the whole way without flinching, in 120 pages, and it is nameable in a sentence. The deduction is the protagonist: Meursault is built not to be rootable, which is the Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes 65 failure - 22 points under Sunrise on the Reaping 87 on that axis alone, same author, same world. The idea payload is what holds this in the 70s rather than the 60s. Print routes are Garamond 2009 (bilingual) and Mlada fronta 1966, plus a Tympanum audiobook.

Reverent allegory is explicitly fine and the ideas are the entire architecture, so nothing here is filtered - but the range is wide because density decides it. Fourteen thousand lines of terza rima carrying fourteenth-century Florentine politics that only footnotes can unlock is the Bidnici 71 penalty at several times the dose. Mikes (Academia 2009) is the readable modern translation; Vrchlicky (Dobrovsky 2013) is not. Reached from the Ukrainian-language score-5 row Bozestvenna komedija, which is not a route.

The idea is good and nameable - a monument on Pluto whose origin nobody can prove, and history as something arguable rather than known. Structure is the risk: three sections, three casts, centuries apart, and no protagonist survives the gaps. The Tolkien pair prices exactly that shape - Silmarillion 80 shows it is survivable when the ideas carry the book, Unfinished Tales 69 shows the cost when the parts stop connecting to each other - and Robinson's sections connect coldly and loosely, which is why this sits nearer the bottom of its range.

t: Jonathan Strange & pan Norrell (Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell)
why: STAYS BLOCKED under the 2026-10-24 re-ruling, on firmer ground than before. The reading that English magic is an invented system is half true: the magicians and their books are Clarke's own, and a faerie bargain or a dead woman raised would by themselves grade as heavy. What fails is the Source test, on practice rather than history. In chapter 21, 'The cards of Marseilles', Childermass and Vinculus lay out tarot spreads and read fortunes from them; Childermass does it successfully at least four times, and a Mythlore study shows the readings, on a lightly altered Tarot de Marseille, predict the novel's events. That is real-world cartomancy performed on the page and shown to work, divination in the seer mould that put Havran 40 at the bottom of the log. It is not alone: Strange raises seventeen dead Neapolitans to interrogate them, necromancy in its original sense, and they answer in 'a dialect of Hell'; the magicians scry for what they cannot see; and Strange drives himself mad with a tincture ground from a mouse that holds a madwoman's madness. No human sacrifice is staged (the gentleman hangs Vinculus as a murder, not a rite), so the veto rests on the Source test alone. Nothing else would have stopped it: no investigation spine, and the opening is one legible situation. The secondary cost, seven hundred dense pages of pastiche and footnotes, stays moot.

t: Neviditelny zivot Addie LaRue (The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue)
why: A bargain with an invented entity, whose terms - nobody can remember her, she cannot say her own name or leave a mark - are declared precisely. That precision is the risk rather than the strength: the profile says rules add obligation, not bonus, and this book is widely argued to bend its own. Addie is rootable and the want is clear. Sexual content is present and treated seriously rather than crudely, which is the axis that matters, but it is central enough to name. Re-examined against the occult ruling of 2026-08-26 (failing EITHER test is a veto, and a rite enacted on the page fails even when the system is invented): the record does not settle it, so the number is unchanged but axis:occult is now a priced risk rather than a cleared question - since the 2026-10-24 re-ruling a bargain with this invented entity struck on the page costs a graded deduction rather than voiding this range. Outstanding check: a bargain with a dark entity struck on the page - the Jonathan Strange ruling treated a faerie bargain as a rite, so this needs the same test.

t: Dvanact povidek o poutnicich (Doce cuentos peregrinos)
why: The stories are built on situations rather than on atmosphere, and several have an idea statable in a phrase - the bar the short-form rule sets, since the suspension removes penalties and never adds points. Marked as a risk on exactly that: in the weaker half the idea dissolves into mood, and short and elegant earns nothing on its own (Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82 are canonical for their ideas, not for their length). Audio edition also exists (Tympanum 2013). Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. Twelve unconnected stories with a shared subject but no shared cast or arc, and the argument for it was the author's craft across the set. That is an average, and the reader does not read an average.

First-person throughout, and moral autonomy against every pressure is a real idea carried by a genuinely rootable narrator - the two things the profile weights most. What keeps it here rather than higher is that the middle third is a sustained romance with the Gothic apparatus around it, and the Moor House section stalls badly. Not filtered on sexual treatment; there is nothing to filter. Covers the duplicate score-5 rows Jana Eyrova (Alpress 2007, Fastrova) and Jane Eyrova (this record); the CooBoo 2019 edition is abridged and is not a route.

t: Starec, ktery cetl milostne romany (Un viejo que leia novelas de amor)
why: A hundred and thirty pages, one setting, one old man, and a clean line about what outsiders do to a place they do not understand. Same bracket as Racek 64-74 and for the same reason: the form is safe, the idea is real but slight, and slightness is what caps it. The title is not what it looks like - the romances are a running joke, not the subject.

The subject is exactly the reader's kind of subject - how a rebellion turns on the people who made it - and the silkpunk world is invented with rules. The method is the problem. Liu writes it in the manner of a dynastic chronicle: omniscient, distant, characters described from outside rather than inhabited, and a cast that keeps widening from the first chapters. That is the opening filter in both its shapes at once - too many lines opened before any is established, and no vantage point from which the reader can tell why any of them matters - and it defeats the protagonist axis at the same time. It is deliberate rather than a flaw, so it will not improve on page fifty. Caropisci 30 is why this is priced hard rather than flagged softly: that book also opened on plenty of incident, and incident without context is what he walked out on. Re-examined against the occult ruling of 2026-08-26 (failing EITHER test is a veto, and a rite enacted on the page fails even when the system is invented): the record does not settle it, so the number is unchanged but occult is a priced risk rather than a cleared question, and an invocation of the book's own gods staged on the page now costs a graded deduction rather than voiding this range. Outstanding check: the gods intervene directly - is any invocation staged on the page?

Genuinely conflicted, and recorded here rather than proposed because of it. Orogeny is declared with real costs and the whole civilisation is organised around it - the declared-capability test passed as thoroughly as in the log's own positives, Hunger Games 89 and Ender's Game 87, and Hugo-winning besides. Against that, the opening is the exact configuration the reader hard-filters on: three named threads braided from chapter one, one of them in second person, with in-world vocabulary used before it is explained. That is the Guards! Guards! 30 shape, and Mortal Engines 55 was abandoned on less. The threads do resolve into one person, but not for hundreds of pages, so the filter could fire long before the payoff. Anyone proposing this must lead with the opening, not with the awards. Discovery (axis:discovery, 2026-10-24): what the world's catastrophe is, what the obelisks are and who the three threads really are, with survival riding on it, the lead's past and the world at once as in Stín věcí ztracených 93 and Project Hail Mary 92; central, so +4. The range stays conditional on the opening: this, or the 30s.

t: General ve svem labyrintu (El general en su laberinto)
why: Bolivar's last river journey, so no magical realism and nothing for the occult filter - straight historical fiction about a man's motives as he loses everything. That is the right axis. The costs are that it assumes a reader who already knows the Gran Colombian collapse, and that the arc is unbroken decline with no counterweight.

t: Pohreb Velke matky (Los funerales de la Mama Grande)
why: Short form, which is the safe category, and the title piece has a real satirical idea. Two reasons it is recorded rather than proposed: several stories run on folk-Catholic supernatural treated as literally true, which is close to the occult filter without clearly tripping it - worth verifying before this is ever offered - and in the weaker pieces the content is atmosphere rather than idea. Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. The occult check on this volume was already outstanding - several pieces run on folk-Catholic supernatural treated as literally true - and the new axis makes an outstanding check on a collection worse than one on a novel: the reader meets whatever is first, and cannot be assumed to read past it.

These stories turn on a dread rather than on a premise, and a mood is not an idea you can name in a phrase - the bar the short-form rule sets, since the suspension removes penalties and never adds points. That is the whole reason for the low range: nothing is wrong with it and little is left behind, which is the Narnia 67 objection. The Elliott family pieces also put witchcraft on the page as family practice; it reads as invented rather than drawn from real occultism, so probably clear of the hard filter, but it needs checking rather than assuming. Re-examined against the occult ruling of 2026-08-26 (failing EITHER test is a veto, and a rite enacted on the page fails even when the system is invented): the record does not settle it, so the number is unchanged but axis:occult is now a priced risk rather than a cleared question - this range is void only if the check below finds the witchcraft drawn from real occultism; an invented family practice enacted on the page now costs a graded deduction instead. Outstanding check: the Elliott family stories - flagged as needing a check since before this ruling and still unchecked. Re-derived 2026-09-03 under the new collection axis: a multi-story book is read from the front and put down on its weakest early pieces, not averaged and not skipped past. Ja, robot 55 is the anchor - the reader stopped after three stories, on the first story's cast and the third story's implausible behaviour, and never reached the pieces the prediction was built on. Already argued down as dread rather than premise, mood not being an idea you can name in a phrase. A collection of moods is the weakest configuration under the new axis: there is no arc to earn patience and no premise to be waiting for.

t: Hvezdy jako prach (The Stars, Like Dust)
why: Early work: a chase with a conspiracy attached rather than a premise worked out, and the author rated it his own weakest. The reveal it builds to - the document that will free the galaxy is the United States Constitution - costs on the heaviest axis instead of paying on it, a galaxy-scale claim asserted rather than earned, which is the Divergent 58 shape of ideas assembled without cohering. Dropped 2026-09-03 under this author's first real score: Ja, robot 55 anchors the protagonist objection for him specifically, and thin people were already the second risk here rather than a hypothetical one. What keeps it off the floor is momentum, a real positive in this log (Hunger Games 89, Red Rising 95), and a lead with one clear want.

t: Sila psa (The Power of the Dog)
why: Motive-driven in the strict sense - the whole book is why Phil is cruel, and the answer is withheld and then earned. But the man whose head the reader lives in is repellent by design, which is the Ballad of Songbirds 65 shape that cost twenty-two points, and the Montana ranch is rendered at length with little happening in it. Sexual content is implicit throughout and handled seriously; that is not the deduction here.

t: Ministerstvo pro budoucnost (The Ministry for the Future)
why: An enormous idea payload and the worst delivery of it for this reader. A hundred-odd chapters, many of them essays, riddles or unattributed eyewitness fragments with no continuing character, and the opening throws several of these forms at once before any thread is established. That is the simultaneous-lines shape of the filter behind three 30s, and the fragments compound it with the second shape, since an unattributed eyewitness voice gives the reader no context to read itself by. The thin-story-spread-thin penalty arrives on top, with no protagonist to offset either - and the protagonist axis outranks whatever it competes with (Artemis 69). Recorded so it is not lost, not proposed.

A hundred and fifty pages, one conceit - anonymous admiring letters, and who we are to the person who loves us - and an ending that retroactively dissolves the plot. The idea is nameable in a phrase, which is what keeps this out of the 50s. Two deductions. The essayistic digressions are the Bidnici 71 penalty in miniature, where the non-plot material is what cost the points. And the erotic preoccupation is treated coldly and instrumentally throughout: not crude, so not a filter, but the same axis that took Artemis 69 down four points from its prediction. Audio edition also exists (Supraphon 2025).

The idea is first-rate and unusual - the American colonies before race had hardened into the thing it became - and Morrison is a better writer than most of this list. It is recorded low purely on the opening: several unnamed first-person voices in dialect, non-linear, with the reader expected to work out who is speaking. That is the filter's own description of what to avoid, and it is the first page rather than a later section.

Lyric vignettes of one summer with almost no plot: heavy description with little story in it, which is a stated deduction and the density penalty at its most concentrated - LOTR 84 was capped for a thin story spread over many pages, and that was with Tolkien's ideas set against it. Here there is no idea nameable in a phrase to set against anything, only nostalgia itself, so the short-form suspension does not apply and would not help if it did. Three print editions held.

The premise is good and the satire lands - a self-governing island of millionaires that tears itself apart over which half owns it - so there is an idea and it has consequences. Everything else is against it: the characters are a quartet of interchangeable musicians used as a camera, and Verne pads with inventory and itinerary, which is the heavy-description deduction.

Two interleaved storylines and both are extended seductions: an eighteenth-century chevalier's night-long, stage-by-stage seduction of a chatelaine at a chateau, and a modern academic's parallel pursuit of a woman at the same chateau turned hotel. The essays on speed, memory and forgetting are commentary layered onto those two narratives, not an independent plot of their own - strip out the two libertine episodes and there is no novel left to narrate, only essays. That is the plot being mainly a sexual pursuit in two historical registers, which the new premise test rejects regardless of the philosophical framing wrapped around it.

Short form, so the character and emotion rules are suspended - but the suspension only removes penalties. Chekhov's declared method is to pose and refuse to answer, which means there is deliberately no idea to carry away, and that is the exact case the profile scores a 3. Recorded so the Chekhov holdings do not keep resurfacing as canonical.

Fifteen stories built on paralysis and the withheld epiphany - eventless by design, and the withholding is the method, so there is deliberately no idea to carry away. That is the case the profile scores a 3: the short form suspends the character and emotion rules, but the suspension only removes penalties, and what earns is an idea left behind (Animal Farm 78, The Little Prince 82). The Dublin specificity adds a comprehension cost on top of that. Canonical and a poor fit; another of the rows that exposed the model's canon bias.

Technically superb domestic realism whose whole aim is a life glimpsed sideways - no premise, no consequences, nothing to think about afterwards, which is the profile's stated earner absent entirely. Nobel prestige is what scored it a 5 in triage, and exclusions are not credentials. Recorded low rather than rejected, because it fails on a graded axis and not on a filter.

t: Pritelkyne z mladi (Friend of My Youth)
why: Domestic realism carried by observation and reticence: nothing is declared, so nothing has to be worked out, and the interest is in what each story withholds. That is the least transferable thing on this reader's axes - what earns here is an idea left behind (Seeking Allah 91, Animal Farm 78, The Little Prince 82) and there is none to name. Recorded low rather than rejected: it fails on a graded axis, not a filter, and clearing the filters is never a reason to propose.

t: Nepritel, pritel, ctitel, milenec, manzel (Hateship, Friendship, Courtship, Loveship, Marriage)
why: Observation and reticence rather than premise and consequence - domestic realism with no idea to name at the end, and an idea left behind is what earns in this log (Seeking Allah 91, Animal Farm 78). Recorded low rather than rejected, because nothing here trips a hard filter. Worth noting that this row was machine-classed romance-maybe on its title alone and ranked -16, near the floor of the mechanical scale, while the model scored it 5: the two signals disagreed completely and both were wrong for different reasons.

Early experimental Hrabal: collage, no plot, no protagonist, and the interest is entirely in the sentence. That is the least transferable thing on this reader's axes - he wants motives on the page (Mockingjay 91) and an idea to take away (Animal Farm 78), and prose that refuses both offers neither. The opening is a real risk on top of that: a text with no legible starting situation is the failure behind three 30s. Also held as Brana 2001.

Anecdote and voice rather than premise and consequence - the monologues are collected for the talk itself, and there is no idea to name at the end of one, which is the bar the short-form rule sets. Nothing trips a hard filter, so this is recorded low rather than rejected. Route note - the only catalogue record under this title is the Popron 2006 audiobook read by Josef Somr and Magdalena Sidonova; the text is in print only inside Spisy 2 (Mlada fronta 2014). This row is also what exposed a bug in the access checker, which matched 'cte' but not 'ctou' and so read an audiobook as print.

Animal stories written for young readers, which is a small pushback rather than the children's filter - Seton wrote them for adults too and they are not simplified - but there is no premise being worked out and the emotional register is straightforwardly sentimental. Recorded low so it stops appearing as an unclassified canonical name.

Prose-poem fragments of a Banat childhood under Ceausescu, deliberately opaque, no plot and no argument - the Nobel citation is for the language. Heavy description with little story in it at maximum concentration, and the fragments do not connect to each other, which is the Unfinished Tales 69 objection. The totalitarian subject is the only thing keeping it off the floor, and the read pair that prices it is Animal Farm 78 against 1984 60: the subject earns when an idea is attached to it and costs when the book is only grim.

t: The City and Its Uncertain Walls
why: No route, and this is the reason it is here rather than in a proposal: the catalogue holds only the English Vintage hardback and no Czech translation exists yet for a 2025 novel. It reached the score-5 list because the pre-model foreign-edition filter was narrowed from 'vintage' to 'vintage books' when that substring was found to be matching Pistorius, so a bare Vintage imprint now slips through. On merit, first assessment of Murakami in this database and a sceptical one: the walled city is declared in detail and then deliberately never explained, which is the undertook-to-explain breach rather than the vague-magic exemption.

t: Inheritance, or, The Vault of souls
why: No route and wrong volume: the catalogue holds only the English Doubleday edition, and it is book four of four with the first three untracked. Recorded to close the row, not as a recommendation. The estimate is for the cycle rather than this volume - rule-bound magic in the ancient language, which pays the worldbuilding axis, against a great deal of borrowed furniture. The chosen-one prophecy is heavily leaned on, but since 2026-10-24 how central a prophecy is costs nothing, only careless or mocking handling, and this one is earnest - that deduction is gone and the range rose two points on it. The live question this raises is volume 1, Eragon, whose Czech availability was not checked.

t: Neuveritelny a tklivy pribeh o bezelstne Erendire a jeji ukrutne babicce (The Incredible and Sad Tale of Innocent Erendira and Her Heartless Grandmother)
why: A short, fable-shaped novella with a nameable idea - a grandmother monetising her granddaughter's body as a debt, and what a person becomes under that arithmetic - told at fairy-tale distance rather than in the room. The content is grim but the treatment is serious rather than crude, which is the axis that docked Artemis 69, and it matches the 'serious rather than crude' reading already logged for Hosseini's child-rape scene. Held on 2026-08-28 with the comparator corrected, and the graded-crudeness axis added to deps - this line argued from that rule without depending on it. Ruled 2026-08-28: The Witcher 53 is a CONFOUNDED row and cannot be cited as a sexual-axis floor - the reader named two independent causes, 'both magic (witches) and the sex was through out the series', and the magic is the occult filter, the most severe objection in the log. The clean crudeness anchor is Ready Player One 55 - 'it was the kind of sex that reduced it that much', the kind and not the amount - with Artemis 69 confirming crudeness costs even in small doses. VOLUME IS UNANCHORED and must not be priced as cheap: Red Rising 95 and Valka stareho muze 87 are BOTH low volume on the reader's own account ('mostly one chapter of a book'), so neither shows what sustained non-crude content costs, and the log's only high-volume row is the confounded one. Note also that VSM's single chapter was still enough to become his one named complaint, so light volume is not free. The old text cited The Witcher 53 alongside Artemis as an axis this book clears; only the Artemis half of that was ever about this axis.

A nameable idea carried a long way: one early harm - the piano teacher's grooming of Roland from 11 to 14, escalating until he seeks her out to lose his virginity before what he believes will be nuclear war - and the book traces its consequence forward across the Cold War, the Wall and Covid, in the same declared-thing-and-its-consequences register the ideas axis credits Animal Farm 78 for. The opening is one concrete situation before it flashes back, so the confusing-opening filter does not fire, and there is no occult and no sustained investigation. This is not a single contained incident: it is one of the three relationships (alongside two marriages) the whole novel is structured around, recurring across the decades as the explanation for Roland's drifting adult life.
